chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Walid, from his father, from his mother Umm Ishaq bint Sulayman, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at me while I was breastfeeding one of my two sons, Muhammad or Ishaq. He said, 'O Umm Ishaq, do not breastfeed him from one breast alone, but breastfeed him from both, so that one becomes food and the other drink.' And the milk of the child of fornication is disliked, as indicated by what has been narrated:

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for breastfeeding an infant according to Shia hadith, and what is the ruling on the milk of a child of fornication?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a practical medical and legal guideline for balanced infant nutrition by nursing from both breasts, while also establishing the *makruh* status of milk from a child of fornication. It serves as a foundational text in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the physical and legal implications of breastfeeding (*radāʿ*) on lineage and inheritance.
